title.narrative: Contributing to Peaceful and Safe Societies 2024-2031' - CIVIC - Advancing Peace and Security: Protecting Civilians in Armed Conflict

description.narrative: CIVIC will strengthen policy and programming for POC so that civilians experience a significant reduction in conflict-related harm.This will be achieved through three interlinked results and key steps across programmes in Mali, Somalia, Yemen, and global policy-research:#1: Civilians bring about improved protection for their communities.#2: Governments and armed actors are responsive to civilian protection needs and concerns, leaving nobody behind and doing no harm.#3: Regional and multinational bodies take concrete steps to improve POC at international, national, and local levels.
Conflict-affected civilians in Somalia, Mali, and Yemen
Partnership with the Netherlands Ministry of Foreign Affairs towards the goal of a significant reduction in conflict-related civilian harm

provider-org.narrative: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Netherlands
Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Netherlands

title.narrative: Result 1: Civilians Bring About Improved Protection For their Communities

description.narrative: Sub-result: Civilians develop and implement joint solutions with government and armed actors to address their protection concernsSub-result: Civilians cultivate, share, and apply knowledge of strategies and tactics for self-protectionSub-result: Civil society organizations and coalitions take collective action to promote the protection of civilians with governments and armed actors

Result 2: Governments and armed actors are responsive to civilian protection needs and concerns, leaving nobody behind and doing no harm

description.narrative: Sub-result: Governments and armed actors directly respond to specific, local protection needs and concerns of civilians through inclusive, and conflict-sensitive approaches (leaving nobody behind and doing no harm)Sub-result: Armed actors and governments demonstrate resolve to improve the protection of civilians through national-level systems, policies, and practicesSub-result: Governments and armed actors engage (inform, consult, coordinate) with civil society to protect civilians

2.1 Number of armed actors (military; security forces, ANSAs) trained on the protection of civilians and civilian harm mitigation
2.2 Percentage of armed actors (military; security forces, ANSAs) members trained on the protection of civilians and civilians harm mitigation reporting increased understanding of POC
Result 3: Regional and Multinational Bodies Take Concrete Steps to Improve the Protection of Civilians at international, national, and community levels

description.narrative: Sub-result: International or regional multinational bodies take concrete, progressive actions to strengthen civilian protection at international, national, and local levels as a result of direct substantive engagement with conflict-affected communities and civilians (E.g., policies, training, reviews, doctrine, SOPs, etc.)Sub-result: International or regional multinational bodies adopt public positions, actions and approaches that establish, reinforce, or improve standards for the protection of civilians in conflict (E.g. through reports, public statements, mandates, policies, votes, strategic reviews, etc.)Sub-result: International or regional bodies, including their field presences on the ground, take concrete steps to improve the protection of civilians and communities in conflict-affected countries (E.g. through diplomacy, programs, policies, training, capacities, mechanisms, or the conduct of multilateral security forces.)

title.narrative: 3.1 Number of concrete steps taken by regional and multi-national bodies influenced by research findings and advocacy activities
Project goal: Strengthen policy and programming for the protection of civilians (POC) so that civilians experience a significant reduction in conflict-related harm
1. Estimated number of civilians in conflict-affected communities (directly and indirectly) experiencing improved POC as a result of CIVIC’s community-based activities.
2. Number of countries where CIVIC activities led to official institutions taking meaningful steps to prioritize the protection of civilians.
3. Number of specific actions taken by governments to address the protection risks inherent in their security sector assistance activities and partnership arrangements.
